manifest.purpose: Evidence manifest for the Otter 1.0 candidate surface. It records what exists, what is documented, what is tested and where they disagree. It does NOT decide what is public.
manifest.authority: Codex owns the public-boundary decision. Every capability is seeded status=candidate, boundaryStatus=unresolved.
manifest.candidateShaNote: Recorded, not chosen here: the Gate 1 candidate Codex nominated. It contains the optimization pass and the event-loop review. The earlier candidate 344db09b is superseded. The public boundary in this manifest is still unresolved.

vocabulary.statusNote: certified requires complete evidence (see tools/Test-OtterReleaseSurface.ps1). Seeds are all candidate.
vocabulary.implementationStateNote: not-referenced means searched and not found; it does NOT mean unsupported. unsupported is used only when a diagnostic or document says so.
vocabulary.hostStateNote: exercised: a test that runs on that host covers the capability. unverified: nothing was run for this capability on that host. Missing is never used to imply support.
vocabulary.reachability: true / false / null. null means not established by the manifest evidence; it is not false.
vocabulary.tokenKindsNote: contract.tokenKinds is empty in seeded entries: token-level evidence (producers, corpus programs, documentation, disposition) is in release/otter-1.0-contract-coverage.json, not linked per capability.

conflictCodes.REACHABILITY_ONLY: listed in STANDARD_LIBRARY_REACHABILITY.md but not in STANDARD_LIBRARY.md
conflictCodes.STDLIB_DOC_ONLY: listed in STANDARD_LIBRARY.md but not in the reachability matrix
conflictCodes.IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY: declared and implemented but in neither document
conflictCodes.NO_DEDICATED_TEST_CASE: in the reachability matrix but no dedicated suite case
conflictCodes.NO_CONTRACT_LINK_FOUND: a documented phrase could not be linked to any contract member
conflictCodes.NO_PROGRAM_IN_CORPUS: no program in the test/conformance/example corpus parses to the linked member
conflictCodes.AREA_NAME_MISMATCH: the reachability matrix and its certification suite name the same area differently

eventContract.note: currentBehavior is the behavior measured BEFORE the decision (docs/OTTER_1_0_EVENT_LOOP_REVIEW.md); decision is the approved contract text. EV2 and EV3 required runtime changes (commit 6451f68).

questions.question: Is cross-source fairness guaranteed or best-effort?
questions.currentBehavior: Fixed per-pass order (watcher, WebSocket, TCP/UDP, HTTP, jobs). No fairness guarantee; command jobs win under load.
questions.decision: Best-effort with eventual progress for ready sources. No equal-share, round-robin, maximum-latency or quantitative fairness guarantee.

questions.question: May one event source drain an unbounded queue before others run?
questions.currentBehavior: Yes for command jobs (while TryDequeue). No for sockets, WebSockets and watchers (one event per source per pass).
questions.decision: No. A source may not do unbounded work while another ready source is waiting; bounded work per turn. The bound is an implementation detail, not language.

questions.question: Which event sources are dispatched during wait?
questions.currentBehavior: Only HTTP and command jobs. Socket, WebSocket and watcher events are held until the main program ends.
questions.decision: Where a target supports wait, wait services every active event source supported by that runtime. Web does not support wait in 1.0 (D101).

questions.question: Is event ordering guaranteed only within a source?
questions.currentBehavior: FIFO within a source; unspecified across sources.
questions.decision: Ordered within a source; cross-source order unspecified.

questions.question: Are TCP/UDP receive callbacks allowed to be delayed by polling cadence?
questions.currentBehavior: Yes: two loop passes per UDP/TCP event and a 10 ms sleep that lasts about 16 ms on Windows (about 31 events/s).
questions.decision: Yes. Polling and scheduling delay are permitted; measured latency and throughput are runtime characteristics, not language semantics.

questions.question: Is the event loop cooperative rather than real-time?
questions.currentBehavior: Cooperative: handlers run to completion on one thread and are never preempted.
questions.decision: Yes. Cooperative: one handler at a time, run to completion, never preempting running Otter code; no real-time guarantee.

questions.question: Are the current scheduling limits documented as part of 1.0?
questions.currentBehavior: Documented in docs/OTTER_1_0_EVENT_LOOP_REVIEW.md only; not in the user documentation.
questions.decision: Measured limits are documented as runtime characteristics (docs/OTTER_1_0_EVENT_MODEL.md), not as the language contract.
